alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 4 at 9:06AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Cocoa to rise
into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to climb to Major
Flood Stage by late this week and remain at Major Flood Stage into
this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Flooding to some roads and water
approaching low lying homes in the Silver Pines subdivision in
Rockledge. Many yards, ditches and pastures flooded and water
approaching low lying structures along Pluckebaum Road in Cocoa and
Rockledge. Flooding to low lying structures in the Lake Washington
area of Melbourne.

- At 8:15 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 16.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

advisories.agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Brevard Public Schools will stay closed for a third day in a row on Wednesday, Nov. 4. A district spokesperson said campus damage, flooded roads and water service outages mean the district can't open safely. District crews are continuing inspections, repairs and cleanup to get campuses ready to reopen.

A flood warning is in effect until 9:30 a.m. Wednesday for some of the hardest-hit parts of Brevard County. Standing water and multiple road closures are still making travel hazardous. Little more rain is expected, but even a small amount could cause problems where floodwater has not drained. Residents in flood-prone areas should stay cautious, avoid driving through standing water and check for road closures before heading out.

advisories.agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
advisories.text: Brevard Public Schools will reopen all campuses on Thursday, Nov. 5, after being closed three days because of the flooding. Buses, before- and after-school care, and after-school activities will run on their normal schedules. Bus routes in storm-affected areas may be delayed. Several Melbourne schools stay under a precautionary boil water notice through the end of the week.
